title: How the Biggest Affirmation App Actually Grows: A Full Teardown of "I am"
description: We measured the biggest affirmation app, I am (738,672 US ratings, 1.82M Instagram followers, 7 posts a day), tore down what it provides and how it grows, and published the full winner-vs-us gap with our own numbers — then copied what is free to copy.
markdown:
# How the Biggest Affirmation App Actually Grows: A Full Teardown of "I am"

*We run Anicca, a small daily affirmation app. This is the first article in our series on becoming experts in our own niche: we measure the winner, publish what we find — wins and losses included — and then copy what works, 100%, except the words themselves.*

*All numbers below were measured on November 12, 2026, from primary sources (the App Store listing, the app's own review feed, and its Instagram account) unless a source is explicitly marked as a third-party estimate.*

---

## The winner, in numbers

**I am – Daily Affirmations** by Monkey Taps has been on the App Store since **May 13, 2014** — twelve and a half years. Today it holds:

- **738,672 ratings on the US App Store, at 4.8 stars** (738,786 by Apple's lookup API the same day)
- **#1 in US search for "daily affirmations", "affirmation", and "positive affirmations"** — all three, measured by us on November 12, 2026. The #2 spot in each is also a Monkey Taps app (Motivation – Daily quotes, ~1.08M ratings)
- **1,819,003 Instagram followers** on @iam.affirmations, with 5,557 posts
- An estimated **~$702K/month in revenue on ~100K US downloads/month** (Airbridge, third-party estimate, October 2026 — not the developer's reported figures)

Here is what its App Store page looks like. Nine screenshots, and the first thing they sell is not meditation, not AI, not a course. It is a widget.

The full set of nine is linked in our research file. The subtitle under the title says it in four words: **"Positive widgets & motivation."**

## What the product actually is

Strip away twelve years of polish and the product is three things:

1. **Pick a focus.** Anxiety, self-love, personal growth, body positivity, work, relationships — you choose categories, and the feed follows.
2. **Get reminded all day.** Notifications on a schedule you set — reviewers mention choosing anything from once a day to once an hour.
3. **Live on the home screen.** A new affirmation on your Lock Screen every day, and a Home Screen widget you glance at without ever opening the app.

That is it. No speaking exercises, no journaling method, no AI coach. Reviewers who have used it for *years* say the same things: it is on their home screen, it greets them every morning, and they share the hourly affirmations with whoever is around. One reviewer found the app on Facebook during a hard period, customized a beach theme, and calls it the best money they ever spent on an app — specifically praising the widget.

The monetization is a classic three-rung ladder, and the ladder is *not broken*:

- **Monthly:** $14.99
- **Yearly:** $59.99 (a 3-day free trial on the yearly plans; a $47.99 yearly variant exists too)
- **Lifetime:** $89.99

Plus one quiet detail we almost missed: the store lists **ten** in-app purchases, including a **$11.99 yearly** plan — a full year priced like a single month. Analysts who track this app call that the hook offer, shown to people who hesitated at the full-price paywall.

The free tier is deliberately tight. Reading the 100 most recent US reviews, the complaints are strikingly consistent: an upgrade ad every few swipes, almost no free wallpapers or icons, and real anger around trial renewals — people who felt a 3-day trial turned into a $60 charge without a clear warning. The winner's weakness is not the product. It is billing trust.

## How it grows

**1. Search is the engine, and the studio owns the shelf.** The app's *title* is the category's biggest keyword. And Monkey Taps doesn't hold the #1 spot with one app — its sister app holds #2. Six apps from the same studio repeat one template (a daily line, a widget, a reminder, a yearly/lifetime paywall) across affirmations, quotes, vocabulary, verses, and facts. The template is the strategy.

**2. Instagram, at volume, with a fixed pattern.** We measured @iam.affirmations directly:

- **7.0 posts per day**
- Format mix: **47% video, 33% image, 20% carousel** — and carousels earn the most likes on average (3,954 in our earlier measurement)
- Every post carries a participation mechanic. On November 11, 2026 — "11/11", a date this audience treats as special — the feed ran the playbook in public:
  - A carousel, **"11 affirmations for 11/11"** (6,630 likes, 75 comments): the final slide asks *"Which one is yours? Comment its number"* — and closes with *"More every morning on the I Am app."* The app pitch lives on the last slide, after the value. [See it here](https://www.instagram.com/p/DfkLrEclnlE/)
  - An image post (5,155 likes, **107 comments**): *"Today is 11/11. Read this four times and mean it. Comment 11:11 to seal it."* [See it here](https://www.instagram.com/p/DfmqkYgEePo/)
  - An image post (1,688 likes) that is simply an argument for the product itself: *"I keep my affirmations on my home screen because I deserve to see supportive words as often as I see noise."* [See it here](https://www.instagram.com/p/Dfmpc63luR7/)

Date events, comment-a-keyword CTAs, save-worthy list carousels, and a bio that funnels to a single link (linktr.ee/iam.app). That is the whole machine, run seven times a day.

**3. The widget is a retention channel that costs nothing.** A third-party teardown of this app (StoreIntel data, October 2026) puts it plainly: users see the widget roughly a dozen times a day, so the product markets itself on the home screen with zero ad spend per impression. The notification plus the widget means the app never has to win your attention back — it never lost it.

**4. Reviews compound.** The rating count grew from 738,546 (Nov 10 snapshot) to 738,672 (Nov 11) to ~738,786 (Nov 12, our measurement) — on the order of **100+ new ratings a day**. Every release note ends with the same line: *"Love the app? Tell us in the reviews section! We read all of them."* And 738K ratings is itself the ASO moat: no newcomer out-ranks that social proof quickly.

**5. Fourteen languages.** The app ships in 14 languages, with localized store listings (in Japan it appears under a Japanese title and holds 1,778 ratings there). The US still produces the majority of revenue (~59% by third-party estimate), but the surface area is global.

**6. Honesty box: they also buy ads.** Trackers recorded 558 active Meta ads for this app in October 2026. Our company rule is free and organic only — paid growth is not something we will copy. We copy the parts that are free: the ASO, the posting system, the widget, the review engine. We record the ads because pretending they don't exist would make this teardown a fairy tale.

## What we learned

1. **The gap is not features. It is distribution volume multiplied by years.** The winning product is *smaller* than we assumed. What it has that we don't is 12.5 years of daily repetition on every surface.
2. **The widget is not a feature. It is the main channel.** Lock Screen + Home Screen + scheduled notifications means the product shows up ~12 times a day without an open.
3. **A price ladder must have a working anchor.** Monthly $14.99, yearly $59.99, lifetime $89.99 — each rung makes the next look rational. An $11.99 "hesitation" yearly offer catches the people the main paywall missed.
4. **Comment mechanics are a format, not a garnish.** "Comment 11:11", "Type YES", "Which number is yours?" — the CTA is built into the creative, tied to the date, every day.
5. **Even the winner bleeds on billing trust.** Trial-renewal anger is the single biggest cluster in its 1-star reviews. Transparent billing is not a differentiator to brag about; it is table stakes the winner is failing — which means it is an opening.

## The gap, in our own numbers (winner vs. us)

We publish our funnel every day, so here is the comparison with our real, measured numbers — same week, no cosmetics:

| Metric | I am | Anicca (us) |
|---|---|---|
| Years live | 12.5 | ~1 |
| US ratings | 738,672 | **1** |
| US search rank, "daily affirmations" | #1 | Not in the top results on any of our 10 tracked keywords |
| Monthly revenue | ~$702K (third-party est.) | **$20 MRR** (RevenueCat, measured; 3 external paying customers) |
| Instagram followers | 1,819,003 | 3 on our English account |
| Posts per day (Instagram) | 7.0 | 2.7 (raised to 7 from Nov 13 — see below) |
| Video share of posts | 47% | ~0% |
| Lifetime price | $89.99 | $59.99 — **the same as our yearly price. Our anchor is broken.** |
| 7-day funnel (Nov 4–10) | Not public | 334 impressions → 14 page views → **1 download**; notification permission **8.0%**; purchases **0** |

That is what a loser-vs-winner gap looks like when you write it down instead of feeling it.

## What we already executed — and what we do next

Already done, before writing this article:

- **Instagram volume corrected to the winner's:** our English account went from 3 slots/day (landing at 2.7) to **7 posts/day**, effective November 13, with the production stock rebuilt to hold that pace.
- **Format mix corrected:** carousel 20% / image 33% / **video 47%** — video was our missing half.
- **ASO hill-climbing loop started:** daily keyword measurement with a positive control, one change at a time, judged after 7 days. Change #001 (the US keyword field) is already applied to our next version, which is in App Store review.

Next, in order:

1. **Fix the lifetime anchor.** Lifetime moves above the yearly price so the ladder reads like the winner's. (Our yearly stays $59.99; lifetime at the same $59.99 is a bug, not a strategy.)
2. **Copy the comment mechanic and the date-event calendar** into our posting production — participation CTA in the creative, tied to dates, with the app pitch on the final carousel slide.
3. **Treat the widget as a channel in our metrics**, the same way we treat Instagram: how many daily glances does it earn, not just "feature shipped."
4. **Add the release-note review line** and keep asking for reviews only after a value moment, in the system dialog — the winner's volume of ratings comes from years of asking, and we will ask for years too, without the trial-renewal traps its reviewers complain about.
5. **Re-measure everything in 7 days** and publish the follow-up with the new numbers, whatever they are.

## Copy this to your agent

If you run an app and want the same teardown of *your* category winner, paste this into your agent (Muse, Grok, Codex — any of them) and run it:

```text
You are my category researcher. Do exactly this, using only free sources:

1. Identify the #1 app in my category by US App Store ratings. Pull its full
   listing with a free scraper (e.g. app-store-scraper): title, subtitle,
   description, version history, release notes, languages, and every
   screenshot URL. Pull its rating count and score with a review tool that
   returns real counts.
2. Read its 100 most recent reviews. Summarize what lovers praise and what
   1-star reviewers complain about, as themes with rough frequencies.
3. List every in-app purchase with prices. Reconstruct the price ladder and
   mark any rung that breaks the anchor (e.g. lifetime priced equal to yearly).
4. Measure its main social account: followers, posts per day over the last
   30 days, format mix (video / image / carousel), average engagement per
   format, and the exact CTA mechanics in its top 10 posts. Save the post URLs.
5. Check its US search rank for the category's 3 biggest keywords.
6. Build a winner-vs-us table using MY measured numbers only (store funnel,
   ratings, followers, posting volume, prices, in-app funnel). Where my
   number does not exist, write "not measured" — never estimate my side.
7. Write the findings as: what they do + the numbers → what we learned →
   what we will change this week, in order. Mark every third-party estimate
   as an estimate. Mark anything you could not get as "not obtained".
8. Save it as a file, share it with the whole team, and schedule a re-run
   in 7 days with the same definitions.
```

We ran exactly this. The research file behind this article — every measurement, source URL, and screenshot link — is kept with our team's working files, and this series continues: the next teardown is already scheduled.

## Our wins and losses, on the record

**Losses:** 1 US rating against the winner's 738,672. A week with 7 total downloads across all six of our apps and zero purchases. A notification permission rate of 8.0% against a category where good onboarding earns 50–65%. A lifetime price set equal to our yearly price. An Instagram account with 3 followers posting 2.7 times a day with almost no video, in a category where the winner posts 7 times a day and half of it is video.

**Wins:** the gap is now measured, not guessed. The volume and format corrections are already live in production. Our ASO loop is running with a first change already in review. And this article exists — the first of a series we will keep publishing, because the knowledge, the experiment results, and the wins and losses compound. That compounding is the whole point: make something people want — a product people want, content people want — and write down what the winners do until we are the ones being torn down.

*Sources: App Store listing for I am – Daily Affirmations (read Nov 12, 2026); Apple iTunes Lookup API; app-store-scraper and appstore-review-cli measurements (Nov 12, 2026); Instagram @iam.affirmations profile and posts via connector (Nov 12, 2026); Airbridge app-revenue and ASO pages (third-party estimates, Oct 2026); apprank.io and apptracker.ai (third-party); I am official blog, blog.theiam.app; our own funnel: full-funnel spec and data v3, Nov 4–10, 2026 window.*
